notes:
Core finding is a reproducible DRIFT in the declared `values` query parameter, not in the response body shape. The contract says: 'Set to true to get each field's configured choices alongside its definition... Left off, the reply is a compact list... omitted.' In practice, query.values=true (and 'true' string, and 1) makes the request fail with HTTP 404 every time (4/4 attempts across two separate calls plus two truthiness variants), while values=false or omitting the param entirely returns 200 cleanly (2/2 and 2/2). So the one lever the contract offers for getting option_values/field_values - the whole reason an agent would call this with the richer form - is broken: an agent that follows the guidance ('Ask for the choices when you intend to write a session') will always get a 404 instead of data. This is worse than a documentation/response-shape mismatch: the documented capability of the endpoint is unreachable.

Secondary finding: the 404 body is a bare {"success":false} with no `error` object at all, contradicting the capability's own declared 400/401/403/404/500 envelope (which requires error.code, error.message, error.details). Same bare-envelope pattern the task flagged for 500s, observed here on 404 instead.

On the base (working) call: response conforms exactly to the declared 200 schema - success, custom_fields, default_fields, nothing missing, nothing extra. But custom_fields was empty on the fixture project, so the richly-nested per-field shape (option_values, field_values, parent_custom_field_id, links, etc. - where drift is most likely per the task's own precedent with update_tag_v1 and get_template_v2) could not be enumerated at all, both because the project has no custom exploratory-session fields configured AND because the only way to request the nested option data (query.values=true) 404s. Could not test an alternate project: the fixture pool only supplies one project (__mcp-capability-fixture__); the v2 identifier form for that same project was rejected client-side on type (contract's declared integer type for project_id is correct - no drift there), and no other project id was available in the pool to try. The contract explicitly frames the endpoint as project-scoped (project_id required path param), not account-scoped, so no account-level variant exists to fall back to.

Net: verdict is DRIFT rather than UNVERIFIED because we have a concrete, reproduced disagreement between declared and actual behavior (the values param), even though the nested item shape itself remains unverified due to the empty fixture project compounded by that same drift.
